diviner_polar_resource_product.provider: NASA LRO Diviner Polar Resource Product (PRP) V2.0
diviner_polar_resource_product.model_observation_period: First year of LRO mapping observations (2010–2011)

aoi.name: Shackleton Rim / ANALOG-X local lunar study window

annual_average_temperature_2cm_below_sur.interpretation: Modelled annual average at 2 cm depth, not a real-time or current surface forecast.

annual_maximum_surface_temperature.interpretation: Modelled annual maximum at the surface.

water_ice_permafrost_stability_depth.meaning: Model-calculated depth at which water ice would sublimate at 1 kg m−2 per billion years. A value of 0 m means the model indicates surface stability. The product reports -999 when the calculated depth exceeds 2.8738 m. This is not a direct detection, concentration, thickness, accessibility or reserve estimate.

limitations: PRP values are model-derived from the first year of mapping observations, not a current operational weather or resource survey.
The mesh uses Kaguya-derived triangular elevation elements, not the same spatial grid or vertical model as the project's LOLA DEM.
The result does not establish ice concentration, mass, purity, mineability, accessibility, or resource reserves.
Temperature/ice-depth statistics are thermal-resource context, not an official landing-site or habitat-safety assessment.

time_weighted.scale_interpretation: Native product byte values interpreted as percentage (0–100); fill values above 100 excluded.
limitations: WAC product is based on one lunar year of observations from 15 Feb 2010 to 5 Feb 2011, with supplementary observations/interpolation.
It is a historical observational illumination-frequency product, not a current or future mission ephemeris simulation.
Near-zero illumination values inside permanently shadowed terrain can be non-zero due to scattered-light and image-noise artefacts.
The low-illumination fraction is a screening proxy, not a formal PSR polygon or regulatory landing-site determination.

low_illumination_proxy_definition.warning: This is not a formal PSR polygon. Official PSR maps and current ephemeris modelling must be consulted for mission engineering.

scientific_boundary: These are historical data products with different epochs and resolutions.
Diviner PRP is a thermal-model product based on the first year of mapping observations.
WAC illumination percentages are based on 2010–2011 imaging; they are not a 2026–2030 ephemeris forecast.
The local terrain support window is 29.6 km square; it does not validate a specific lander footprint.
Ice stability depth does not equal a direct measurement of ice abundance, concentration, thickness or extractability.
LOLA DEM interpolation and measurement count support remain separate quality dimensions.
